title: Haircuts for a Round Face: Adding Height and Angles
hero_alt: Close-up of a man with a round face and short hair, poolside
card_text: Shorter sides and height on top lengthen a round face. Which style pages to show your barber, and what to skip.
lede: The haircuts that flatter a round face add height on top and keep the sides short. That combination makes the head look longer and narrower, which balances the softer angles of a round face. A skin fade with a textured top, a hard part with some lift, or a textured crop with height at the front all work. Cuts that add width at the sides, or sit flat and rounded on top, tend to make a round face look rounder.
Here's how to think about it, three style pages worth showing me, and the shapes to skip.

seo.description: Haircuts for a round face, from a Carlsbad, NM barber: short sides and height on top to lengthen the face, which styles to show and what to avoid.

blocks.heading: Vertical, not horizontal.
paragraphs: A round face has similar width and length, fuller cheeks and a softer jaw. A haircut can't change the face, but it changes the outline around it.
Height on top stretches that outline upward. Short sides pull it in at the widest point. Together they shift the overall shape from a circle toward an oval.
Angles help as well. A part, a crisp line or a fade with a clear edge adds structure that a round face doesn't supply on its own.
A quick test: look at your face straight on and notice where it's widest. On a round face that's usually the cheeks, which is exactly where the sides of the haircut sit.

blocks.heading: Three pages to start from.
blocks.lead: Each one adds height or angles.

items.title: Skin fade with a textured top
items.body: Sides taken to skin so they're as narrow as possible, with height left on top. The contrast does most of the lengthening.

items.title: Hard part
items.body: A shaved part line adds a sharp angle, and a top swept up and to the side adds height. Structure for a soft face shape.

items.title: Textured crop with lift
items.body: A crop works when it's cut with height at the front instead of lying flat. Keep the sides tight and the texture pointing up.

blocks.heading: Shapes that round it out.
paragraphs: A round face isn't a problem to fix, but a few shapes do it no favors:
bullets: Puffy or long sides, which widen the face at its fullest point.
A blunt fringe cut straight across, which shortens the face.
A flat, rounded top with no height, like a bowl.
Chin-length cuts that end right at the cheeks.

blocks.heading: Can you wear one?
paragraphs: A fringe isn't off limits. A textured, broken-up fringe that's angled or swept to one side keeps some vertical movement, like the heavy textured fringe in the photo above. The version to avoid is a dense, straight-across line that cuts the face in half.
If you love a forward style, keep the sides very tight so the width stays under control.
The part helps too. A deep side part swept up and over adds height and an angle at once. A center part with flat sides tends to widen the face.

blocks.heading: Use both ends.
paragraphs: A beard with more length at the chin and shorter cheeks lengthens a round face from below, the same way height does from above. The Signature Cut ({{price:signature-cut}}, {{minutes:signature-cut}}) handles the haircut and a beard trim or line-up in one visit.

items.q: What haircut suits a round face?
items.a: One with short sides and height on top, like a skin fade with a textured top or a hard part with lift.

items.q: Should guys with round faces keep their hair short?
items.a: Short on the sides, yes. The top usually looks better with some length for height.

items.q: Do fades work on round faces?
items.a: Yes. Tight sides narrow the widest part of the face.

items.q: Is a buzz cut good for a round face?
items.a: It can be, especially with a high fade. With no height on top, it relies on the sides staying tight.

blocks.heading:
Height up top.
